court: Franklin County Court of Common Pleas, General Division, State of Ohio. Three related matters, all read directly from the clerk's docket and from the filed PDFs.
case_number: 23 CV 005498 (the contract suit, 'TAS Litigation'); 23 CV 008152 (the fraudulent-transfer suit); 23 JG 090221 (certificate of judgment / garnishment proceeding on the 23CV005498 judgment)
plaintiff: JobsOhio, 41 S. High Street, Suite 1500, Columbus, OH 43215, pleaded as 'a private non-profit corporation organized and in good standing under the laws of the State of Ohio.' Not JobsOhio Beverage System and not the State of Ohio. Counsel in 23CV005498: Robert J. Mann and Mary Spahia-Carducci, Mann & Carducci Co. LPA. Counsel in 23CV008152: Robert C. Folland and Samantha R. Pugh, Barnes & Thornburg LLP.
defendants: 23CV005498: Olive AI, Inc., 99 East Main St., Columbus, OH 43215 (sole defendant). Pleaded as a Delaware corporation registered to do business in Ohio, 'formerly named CrossChx, Inc., before changing its name to Olive AI, Inc. on or about August 27, 2020.' No attorney ever appeared for it.
23CV008152 as originally filed 2023-11-15: Olive AI, Inc.; Brock A. Wanless; Waystar Technologies, Inc.; Humata Health, LLC

23CV008152 as of the Second Amended Complaint filed 2024-06-05: Olive AI, Inc.; Brock A. Wanless; Waystar Technologies, Inc.; Humata Health, LLC; Wild Ginger Holdings, LLC; Sean Lane; and Brian Rutkowski
23JG090221: Olive AI, Inc. as judgment debtor

allegations.program_or_agreement: NOT a grant. The money was provided under a 'Talent Acquisition Services Agreement' (TAS Agreement) dated on or about 2020-04-08 between JobsOhio and Olive AI, Inc. (then CrossChx), amended by an 'Amendment to Talent Acquisition Services Agreement' dated on or about 2020-05-29 that replaced Exhibit A. Under it JobsOhio did not hand money to the company. JobsOhio agreed to fund subcontractors and outside parties who performed services for the company 'up to the amount of $645,000.00,' and the company agreed to repay JobsOhio the cost of those services if it missed its commitments. The complaint describes the services as 'marketing and attraction services, creative concepting, digital advertising, social media advertising, sponsorship events, coding bootcamp, talent acquisition, and other services as specified therein.' The complaint calls this 'one of its incentive offerings' and does not name any of JobsOhio's 12 published programs. This is a likely explanation for why the Form 990 Schedule I payments match no entry in the monthly executed grants reports.
allegations.breach_alleged_23CV005498: Count I, Breach of TAS Agreement. Olive AI missed its Metric Commitments at the Metric Evaluation Date of 2021-12-31. Per its own 2022 Annual Report filed under the TAS Agreement, Olive AI 'had only created 65 new jobs instead of the 100 new jobs required under the TAS Agreement, and the new jobs had an associated payroll of $9,889,289.00 instead of the required $10,000,000.00.' JobsOhio sent a demand letter dated 2023-06-15 (Exhibit 1 to the complaint) requiring repayment by 2023-07-15; Olive AI did not pay.
allegations.allegations_23CV008152: Fraud and fraudulent transfer. JobsOhio alleges Olive AI and its officers conducted 'sham settlement negotiations' through the fall of 2023 to stall a default judgment while Olive AI sold its business lines, then shut down, created Olive/ABC LLC in California on 2023-11-01 and on 2023-11-03 executed an assignment for the benefit of creditors transferring its remaining assets to Olive/ABC, placing them 'outside the reach of JobsOhio.' The court's 2024-05-10 order records JobsOhio's allegation that 'Olive AI received approximately $50 million in the sale, but failed to pay JobsOhio.' Counts in the Second Amended Complaint include fraudulent conveyance as to Wanless, Rutkowski and Lane (Counts V and VI), civil conspiracy to effect the fraudulent transfers as to Lane, Wanless and Rutkowski (Count VII), fraud actual and constructive as to Olive, Wanless, Lane and Rutkowski (Count VIII), piercing of corporate veil / alter ego as to Sean Lane (Count IX), and unjust enrichment as to all defendants (Count X).
allegations.asset_sale_prices_pleaded_in_23CV008152: Waystar paid $10,000,000 for the Patient Access Business; Humata Health paid $1,250,000 for the Prior Authorization Business (a footnote says the asset purchase agreement was with Sequi Ventures LLC dba Humata); Wild Ginger Holdings paid $1,000,000 in cash for common stock in the five incubator startups and $50,000 for roughly 25 desks, 40 monitors and a 2009 Ford cargo van. JobsOhio alleged laid-off Olive employees received about $10,000 each while Wanless and Rutkowski received 'bonuses' of $879,000 and $820,000 around the same time. The complaint also alleges Olive created Olive (Assignment for the Benefit of Creditors) LLC in California on 2023-11-01 and assigned its remaining assets to it on 2023-11-03, and that Olive engaged Paladin Management Group for the wind-down.
allegations.settlement_history_on_the_record: The 23CV008152 exhibits reproduce the 2023 settlement correspondence. Olive AI's opening offer (Exhibit 1, 2023-08-18) asked JobsOhio to forgive one third, $199,473.39, arguing 'Olive exceeded jobs/payroll targets for much of the past 3 years' and 'narrowly missed the targets in '22 (achieved 98.9% of the payroll target).' JobsOhio countered at $400,000.00 (Exhibit 2, 2023-08-21). A draft Settlement Agreement and Release for $400,000.00 was negotiated but never signed; its signature blocks are blank. It would have required Olive AI to execute an Agreed Judgment Entry for $598,420.17 that JobsOhio could file without notice on nonpayment.

amount_sought: $598,420.17, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees and costs. The figure is JobsOhio's actual subcontractor and outside-party spend under the TAS Agreement, not the $645,000.00 cap. In 23CV008152 JobsOhio sought the same $598,420.17 '(less any amounts recovered by JobsOhio in this proceeding or the TAS Litigation)' plus punitive damages in excess of $25,000.00.
job_commitments: From the complaint, paragraph 5: Olive AI was 'obligated in turn to meet specified metrics for job creation, job retention, and minimum payroll requirements at the Project Site. These metrics obligations required Defendant to create 100 new jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $10,000,000.00, and to retain 75 jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $6,435,854.00. (Hereinafter the "Metric Commitments").' Metric Evaluation Date 2021-12-31; Metric Expiration Date 2023-12-31. Reported performance as of 2021-12-31: 65 new jobs created and $9,889,289.00 of associated payroll.

repayment_provision_quote.note: These are the only verbatim excerpts of a JobsOhio agreement's repayment terms on the public record in these cases, and they appear in exactly one document: JobsOhio's own complaint in 23CV005498 (filed 2023-08-02, pages 3 and 4). The later and much longer Second Amended Complaint in 23CV008152 does not quote the agreement at all, it only paraphrases it, so the 2023-08-02 complaint is the single source. The agreement itself is not attached to either. Emphasis italics in the original are not reproduced here; the complaint adds '(Emphasis added).' after each block.
repayment_provision_quote.section_2b_obligations_of_company: Obligations of Company. JobsOhio has approved provision of the Deliverables and Services to the Company to induce Company to undertake and complete the Project, with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans at the Project Address above. Accordingly, the Company's completion of the Project, maintaining substantial operations (as defined in Section 9(a)(iv)) at the Project Address, and achieving, at the Project Address, Company's Metric Commitment obligations set forth on the first page of this Agreement during the Term are each essential terms of this Agreement. Company hereby agrees that it:
repayment_provision_quote.section_2b_i: (i) Must attain all Metric Commitments no later than the Metric Evaluation Date, and once met, must maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date.
repayment_provision_quote.section_9a_ii_paraphrased_not_quoted: The complaint states, in its own words rather than as a quotation, that 'Section 9(a)(ii) of the TAS Agreement provides that Defendant is in breach and default of the TAS Agreement if Defendant fails to comply with the Metric Commitments.'
repayment_provision_quote.section_9b_remedies: *** In the event of a Breach by Company, JobsOhio may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: (i) Discontinue all Deliverables and Services; (ii) Liquidated Damages. As liquidated damages, Company shall pay JobsOhio upon demand the value of each category of Service and/or Deliverable listed on the Talent Acquisition Services Value Allocation in Exhibit A that has been performed, whether or not completed, at the time of the Breach; or (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies JobsOhio may have under this Agreement or applicable law.
repayment_provision_quote.demand_letter_2023_06_15: From Exhibit 1 to the complaint, a JobsOhio letterhead letter signed by Don Grubbs, General Counsel, to Brian Rutkowski, Chief Administrative Officer of Olive AI: 'In its 2022 Annual Report, however, OliveAI reported it had created only 65 new jobs with an associated payroll of $9,889,289 at the Project Site. Pursuant to Section 9(a) of the Agreement, OliveAI is therefore in breach of its Metric Commitments. As a result, and pursuant to Section 9(b)(ii) of the Agreement, JobsOhio demands that OliveAI repay to JobsOhio as liquidated damages the service value performed under the Agreement in the amount of five hundred ninety-eight thousand four hundred twenty dollars and seventeen cents ($598,420.17). The amount demanded to be repaid takes into account the number of jobs OliveAI created, the total fixed assets invested in the Project, as well as the market conditions and other factors provided by OliveAI to JobsOhio.'
repayment_provision_quote.secondhand_recital_of_the_same_terms: A draft settlement agreement filed as Exhibit 10 to the Second Amended Complaint in 23CV008152 recites the deal in one sentence: 'WHEREAS, JobsOhio and Olive entered into a Talent Acquisition Services Agreement ("TAS Agreement") pursuant to which JobsOhio agreed to provide, among other matters, marketing and attraction services, creative concepting, digital advertising, social media advertising, sponsorship events, coding bootcamp, talent acquisition, and other services as specified therein up to the amount of $645,000.00, with Olive agreeing that it would repay all such costs if it failed to achieve Metric Commitments for new job creation, existing job retention, and specified payroll amounts as of specific Metric Evaluation and Metric Expiration dates at is facility located at 99 East Main Street, Columbus, Ohio, 43215, (hereinafter referred to as the "Project Site"), as set forth in the TAS Agreement, and;' The typo 'at is facility' is in the original.

sean_lane.added: yes, in case 23CV008152 only, not in the contract suit
sean_lane.timeline: Sean Lane was not a defendant when 23CV008152 was filed on 2023-11-15. JobsOhio filed a Motion to File Amended Complaint on 2024-04-22. The court granted it on 2024-06-05 and the Second Amended Complaint naming Lane was filed the same day. This confirms the news-based lead that JobsOhio moved in April 2024 to add Lane, and pins the dates.
sean_lane.counsel: Thompson Hine LLP (Muna Abdallah, Thomas W. Palmer)
theories: Count VI, fraudulent conveyance as to Sean Lane, under Ohio Rev. Code 1336.04(A)(1) and 1336.04(A)(2). JobsOhio alleged five startups spun out of Olive (Circulo, Healia, Seam Technologies, Rotera and Magenta Care Continuum), that 'the Incubator Companies were being created by and/or used by Lane to divest Olive technology and assets,' that they 'received property and/or assets of Olive ... at the direction and authorization of Sean Lane,' and that the transfers 'were ultimately received by and used by Sean Lane as the equity interests of the Incubator Companies were sold to Wild Ginger.'

Count VII, civil conspiracy to effect the fraudulent transfers, as to Lane, Wanless and Rutkowski: 'The Individual Defendants conspired with one another to take valuable assets from Olive and fraudulently transfer them to Waystar, Humata, Wild Ginger, and themselves for the unlawful purpose of hindering, delaying, and defrauding JobsOhio.'

Count VIII, fraud (actual and constructive), as to Olive, Wanless, Lane and Rutkowski, for 'repeatedly and falsely representing that JobsOhio would be paid upon the closing of transactions being contemplated by Olive ... when said Defendants were not in fact working on any such arrangements, and never had any intention of signing or honoring such an agreement.'

Count IX, piercing of corporate veil / alter ego, as to Sean Lane. JobsOhio alleged Lane 'utilized the corporate funds of Olive to purchase, pay rent, and/or make improvements to certain property owned by Wild Ginger known as the Worthington Inn located at 649 High Street, Worthington, Ohio,' that he is the sole member of Wild Ginger Holdings LLC, and that he 'used his position as CEO to undercapitalize Olive so that it would not be able to satisfy any judgments obtained against it.' Prayer item D sought 'a declaratory judgment piercing the corporate veil of Wild Ginger to impose liability on Lane, individually, for the amount of the fraudulent transfer provided to Wild Ginger.'
Count X, unjust enrichment, as to all defendants.
sean_lane.outcome_for_lane: Never adjudicated. JobsOhio dismissed the action against Lane with prejudice on 2024-11-19. No finding of liability was ever made against him, and the docket records none.

status.23CV005498: Closed. Olive AI never appeared or answered. JobsOhio moved for default judgment on 2023-10-26. On 2023-11-20 Judge Andria C. Noble signed an 'Entry Granting Plaintiff JobsOhio Judgment Against Defendant Olive AI, Inc.' ordering 'that JobsOhio is granted judgment against Defendant Olive AI, Inc., in the amount of $598,420.17, plus costs and statutory interest from the date of this Judgment.' On 2024-11-19 JobsOhio filed a Satisfaction of Judgment stating the judgment 'has been fully satisfied and is hereby released.'
status.23CV008152: Closed. Judge Kim J. Brown denied all four motions to dismiss on 2024-05-10. JobsOhio partially dismissed certain parties on 2024-03-19 and again on 2024-11-12. On 2024-11-19 JobsOhio filed a Notice of Dismissal: 'Pursuant to Ohio Rule of Civil Procedure 41(A)(1)(a), Plaintiff JobsOhio hereby dismisses this action, with prejudice, against Defendants Humata Health, Inc., Waystar Technologies, Inc., Olive AI, Inc., Brock A. Wanless, Sean Lane, and Brian Rutkowski. Each Party shall bear its own attorneys' fees and costs.' The case was terminated the same day.
status.23JG090221: Still carried as ACTIVE on the clerk's system. JobsOhio filed a certificate of judgment on 2023-11-22 and ran about ten bank garnishments in February and March 2024. The one garnishee answer whose detail is on the public docket, Cooper State Bank on 2024-03-20, reads 'NO ATTACHED FUNDS AVAILABLE.' A service attempt on 2025-03-25 failed with the reason 'VACANT' at 99 E Main St.
status.appeal: None. No Tenth District appellate case appears under the JobsOhio party name.

amount_recovered: The $598,420.17 judgment was fully satisfied and released on 2024-11-19, the same day JobsOhio dismissed the fraud case with prejudice with each side bearing its own fees. The record therefore establishes that JobsOhio recovered the full judgment amount. No filing states the dollar figure actually paid, who paid it, or the terms of any settlement, and no settlement agreement was filed. Judgment interest and costs accrued from 2023-11-20 but no filing quantifies them. Do not state a recovery figure other than 'the judgment of $598,420.17 was recorded as fully satisfied.'
agreement_is_exhibit: No. This is a firm negative, read directly from the filing. The complaint in 23CV005498 says twice, at paragraphs 5 and 9: 'A copy of the TAS Agreement is not attached as it contains confidential and/or competitive and/or trade secret information, and as Defendant already has a copy in its possession,' and 'A copy of the Amended TAS Agreement is not attached hereto as it contains confidential and/or competitive and/or trade secret information, and as Defendant already has a copy in its possession.' The only exhibit to that complaint is Exhibit 1, the 2023-06-15 demand letter. The 73-page Second Amended Complaint in 23CV008152 attaches 17 exhibits, all of them settlement emails, an unsigned draft settlement agreement, two Columbus Business First articles and the WARN Act notice. None is the TAS Agreement. An 'Agreed Judgment Entry' referenced in the draft settlement is also not in the record. One docket entry, 2024-04-17, reads 'DOCUMENT SEALED BY COURT' alongside an agreed order and a discovery order, so some material in that case is sealed and was not reviewed.
confidence: High. Every fact above was read from the Franklin County Clerk of Courts docket and from the filed PDF images themselves, retrieved on 2026-11-03: the complaint, the demand letter, the default judgment entry, the satisfaction of judgment, the Second Amended Complaint and its 17 exhibits, the order denying the motions to dismiss, and the notice of dismissal. Nothing here rests on a news summary.

notes.headline_for_the_post: This is the public place where a JobsOhio agreement's repayment terms appear in the agreement's own words. The quoted Section 2(b) and Section 9(b) language above is the strongest available answer to what JobsOhio's individual agreements actually require, as against what the 12 published program guidelines disclose.
notes.important_caveat_on_generalizing: The Olive AI agreement is a Talent Acquisition Services Agreement, not a cash grant agreement. JobsOhio paid subcontractors directly and the company owed repayment of the service value. Its remedy is styled 'Liquidated Damages,' not a clawback of a grant. Do not present these sections as the text of a JobsOhio grant agreement. Present them as the repayment terms of a JobsOhio incentive agreement, which is what the filing supports.
notes.why_the_990_numbers_do_not_match: Olive AI's three Form 990 Schedule I receipts total $560,770 (FY2020 $135,895 as CROSSCHX INC, FY2021 $402,375 as OLIVE, FY2022 $22,500 as OLIVE AI INC). JobsOhio pleaded that it 'incurred $598,420.17 in subcontractor and/or outside party costs' under the TAS Agreement. The two figures are close but not equal and cover different periods and different reporting bases, and the court record does not reconcile them. Do not assert that the Schedule I payments are the same money as the $598,420.17 without saying the record does not connect them.
notes.correction_to_the_prior_lead: The earlier news-headline-based lead said JobsOhio sued after Olive AI shut down. That is wrong on the contract suit. JobsOhio sued on 2023-08-02, nearly three months before the 2023-10-31 shutdown announcement, and had its default judgment on 2023-11-20. The suit that followed the shutdown is the separate fraudulent-transfer case filed 2023-11-15. The April 2024 Sean Lane detail is correct: motion filed 2024-04-22, granted and pleading filed 2024-06-05.
notes.bigger_finding_for_the_project: The same party-name search returned 89 Franklin County matters involving JobsOhio from 2011 through 2026: 62 civil suits with JobsOhio as plaintiff, 23 judgment and certificate-of-judgment matters, and a handful where JobsOhio is the defendant. Named defendants include Therma-Tru Corp (21CV001186), Republic Steel (23CV008186), Graphic Packaging International (20CV000832), Lincoln Electric Automation (22CV006725), Nexient LLC (23CV005495, filed the same day as the Olive AI suit), S & P Data Ohio (23CV008583), Treves Inc (24CV004104), Mike-Sells Potato Chip Co (23CV008049) and about fifty more. JobsOhio filed at least 13 new ones in October to December 2025 and at least 11 more in 2026. There is also one suit running the other way, VET MENTOR AI INC -VS- JOBSOHIO ET AL (26CV006007, filed 2026-06-26, still ACTIVE). Every one of these dockets is retrievable the same way, and each complaint will quote the repayment provision of that company's agreement. A full list is saved at data/research3/jobsohio_franklin_cases.csv. This is a much larger story than the single Olive AI case.
what_could_not_be_established: The full text of the TAS Agreement. It is not in either court file, by JobsOhio's express choice, on confidentiality and trade-secret grounds.
The dollar amount actually paid to satisfy the judgment, who paid it, and whether any settlement payment exceeded or fell short of $598,420.17 plus interest. No settlement agreement was filed.
What is in the material sealed by the court on 2024-04-17 in 23CV008152.
Which of JobsOhio's 12 published programs, if any, this agreement sits under. The complaint calls it 'one of its incentive offerings' and never names a program.

Article text from Columbus Business First, Axios Columbus and the Columbus Dispatch. Only RSS headlines and dates were retrieved; direct fetches are paywalled and the Wayback Machine was not attempted because the docket answered the questions directly.
notes.method: The Franklin County Clerk's Case Information Online system requires accepting a disclaimer to open a session, then posts a party-name search to /nameSearch and case dockets to /caseSearch. Document images are served as scanned PDFs from /imageLinkProcessor/docimages/court/CV/fiche/<fiche>/frame/<frame>/pages/<n>. The PDFs are CCITT fax images with no text layer and were rendered to PNG with PyMuPDF and read as images. The site asks that it not be used for bulk extraction; this was a small number of targeted queries for one company.
